draft.title: Cumulative distribution functions
card: The cumulative distribution function (CDF), F(x), gives P(X ≤ x). It is the area under the density curve f from the lowest value of X up to x.
Find it by integrating: F(x) = ∫ f(t) dt, from the lowest value up to x. Use t inside the integral so x is only the upper limit.
Worked example: f(x) = 2x for 0 ≤ x ≤ 1. Then F(x) = ∫ 2t dt from 0 to x = x². So P(X ≤ 0.5) = 0.5² = 0.25.
F rises from 0 to 1 and never falls. For an interval, P(a ≤ X ≤ b) = F(b) − F(a). Differentiating F gives back f.
draft.remember: F(x) is the area so far: integrate f up to x.

a.q: A variable has density f(x) = 2x for 0 ≤ x ≤ 1. What is P(X ≤ 0.6)?
a.why: F(x) = x², so P(X ≤ 0.6) = 0.6² = 0.36. Substituting 0.6 into f gives 1.2, which is the height of the curve, not the area up to 0.6.

b.q: A variable has density f(x) = 2x for 0 ≤ x ≤ 1. What is P(0.5 ≤ X ≤ 0.8)?
b.why: F(x) = x², so P = F(0.8) − F(0.5) = 0.64 − 0.25 = 0.39. Using F(0.8) alone gives 0.64, which wrongly includes the area below 0.5.
b.clue: Subtract the area up to 0.5 from the area up to 0.8.

final.title: Cumulative distribution functions
card: The cumulative distribution function (CDF), \(F(x)\), gives \(P(X \le x)\). It is the area under the density curve \(f\) from the lowest value of \(X\) up to \(x\).
Find it by integrating: \(F(x) = \int f(t) \, dt\), from the lowest value up to \(x\). Use \(t\) inside the integral so \(x\) is only the upper limit.
Worked example: \(f(x) = 2x\) for \(0 \le x \le 1\). Then \(F(x) = \int_{0}^{x} 2t \, dt = x^{2}\). So \(P(X \le 0.5) = 0.5^{2} = 0.25\).
\(F\) rises from 0 to 1 and never falls. For an interval, \(P(a \le X \le b) = F(b) - F(a)\). Differentiating \(F\) gives back \(f\).
final.remember: \(F(x)\) is the area so far: integrate \(f\) up to \(x\).

a.q: A variable has density \(f(x) = 2x\) for \(0 \le x \le 1\). What is \(P(X \le 0.6)\)?
a.why: \(F(x) = x^{2}\), so \(P(X \le 0.6) = 0.6^{2} = 0.36\). Substituting 0.6 into \(f\) gives 1.2, which is the height of the curve, not the area up to 0.6.

b.q: A variable has density \(f(x) = 2x\) for \(0 \le x \le 1\). What is \(P(0.5 \le X \le 0.8)\)?
b.why: \(F(x) = x^{2}\), so \(P = F(0.8) - F(0.5) = 0.64 - 0.25 = 0.39\). Using \(F(0.8)\) alone gives 0.64, which wrongly includes the area below 0.5.
b.clue: Subtract the area up to 0.5 from the area up to 0.8.

wants.why: It shows F rising from 0 to 1 as the area under f builds up.
